la:verb:vomo.html:
vŏmo, ŭi, ĭtum, 3, v. n. and a.
[Sanscr. vām-ami, vomit; Gr. ἐμέω; root ϝεμ].
Neutr., to puke, spew, throw up, vomit (a common method among the Romans of renewing the appetite).
Lit.: cum vomere post cenam te velle dixisses,; ; ; ; : in mensam,.—With a homogeneous object: vomitum,.—Impers. pass.: ab horā tertiā bibebatur, ludebatur, vomebatur,.—
Transf., in gen., to pour forth, empty: quā largius vomit (Padus), discharges itself into the sea, .—
Act., to throw up or discharge by vomiting; to vomit up or forth (cf.: eructo, nauseo).
Lit.: sanguinem,: paene intestina sua,.—
Transf., in gen., to vomit forth, i. e. to throw or pour out in abundance; to emit, discharge (poet.): (Charybdis) vomit fluctus totidem totidemque resorbet,: undam,: fumum,: geminas flammas,: mel (apes),: vitam,to breathe out,; so, animam,: argentum,to give up,: armataeque vomunt stridentia tela fenestrae,: pinguem nebulam vomuere lucernae,.
la:verb:vomo.inflection: ŭi, ĭtum, 3, v. n. and a.
